result.title: Ascent Conditions for Length-Normalized Single-Rollout Policy Updates
result.comment: 16 pages, 1 figure, 3 tables; code and data included as ancillary files
result.summary: Dividing each trajectory's score contribution by its realized length can change the direction of a reward-centered policy update. In a finite trajectory model, we derive an exact ascent threshold for a three-outcome softmax policy and exhibit a binary-reward example in which the expected Euclidean update decreases task success. Natural-gradient ascent holds for fully controllable outcome distributions with deterministic binary labels, but can fail under a one-parameter restriction. A third-order U-statistic estimates the first-order return change without bias from independent current-policy trajectories, one per request. In the example, a same-sample plug-in estimator instead has the opposite sign in expectation for batch sizes two through forty-nine. Exact policy-grid enumeration confirms the local sign reversal. In a branching process, length-normalized learning initially loses return, then recovers and exceeds the unnormalized comparator. The analysis concerns the expected update field at the current policy.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在有限轨迹模型下研究将每条轨迹分数贡献除以实际长度后的策略更新方向，为三结果 softmax 策略推导出精确上升阈值，并给出长度归一化导致期望更新反而降低任务成功率、局部符号反转的二元奖励例子，另提出无偏的三阶 U 统计量估计一阶回报变化。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「长度归一化会改变策略更新方向」的结论，可供核查在长链推理（含 latent 或文本轨迹）上做长度归一化训练时，贡献分配与信用分配是否出现类似偏差。
